newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran president starts term on conciliatory note.
newsitem.headline: Iran president starts term on conciliatory note.

text.p: Mohammad Khatami launched his presidency on Sunday with a call for cooperation among Iran's ruling clergy and other domestic forces and hinted at readiness to deal with world powers.

Accepting Iran's highest elective office after confirmation by supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Khatami said Iran's problems required "cooperation and coordination between the great scholars of this country" and various other forces.
"We need each and every person of this great nation, the women, the men, the youth...," he said in a ceremony at Khamenei's official residence.
In what appeared to be a message to the West, Khatami said "Iran is for peace and security and it has a message of spirituality for all the people of the world...
"Based on wisdom (Iran) will shake hands with the people of the world maintaining its Islamic dignity and national honour."
But he reiterated the Islamic republic's attack on "expansionist" policies -- seen as a reference to Iran's arch-foes the United States and Israel.

The ambassadors of European Union countries -- absent from Tehran in a diplomatic dispute over German court charges of high Iranian involvement in political assassinations -- did not attend the ceremony.
Diplomats said Iran and the EU were engaged in last-minute efforts to try to get the ambassadors back in time for Khatami's oath-taking on Monday.
A foreign ambassador who did attend Sunday's ceremony said: "I think his speech was conciliatory on the whole rather than confrontational".
Khatami, 54, was elected in May by an overwhelming majority led by the youth and women eager to stop a conservative, parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, from taking over.

Outgoing president Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, handing over the presidency, said Khatami had the right credentials, the trust of Khamenei and "a very large vote of the people to confront with confidence the aggressive and arrogant powers, especially the United States and Israel".

Repeated attacks against Iran's declared enemies are mainstays of the 18-year Islamic revolution. A painting on one entire side of a nine-storey building in the capital shows skulls and dropping bombs in the place of the U.S. Stars and Stripes flag and the legend "Death to America".

Khamenei, in a confirmation decree read by Rafsanjani, said: "I appoint him (Khatami) President of the Islamic Republic of Iran...as long as he is committed, and I am sure he will be committed, to the Islamic path and defending the oppressed."

Khamenei, flanked by Khatami and Rafsanjani, lashed out against remarks by analysts and news agencies which reported that the large turnout for Khatami was a sign Iranians had turned their backs on the revolution.

"They are saying the people are separated from their system and revolution...This is not correct...The people are with the Imam," said Khamenei in front of a picture of revolutionary leader the late Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini hanging on the wall.

"Let them say what they want and analyse as they wish. These news agencies which follow the Zionists do not know this people, do not know our country or our officials. They do not know the extent of the wrong they are doing," he added.
